name: dbl_to_dbl_fcnvfxt
prose: Function dbl_to_dbl_fcnvfxt(srcptr, _nullptr, dstptr, status) converting the double at srcptr to a signed 64-bit integer at dstptr by truncation toward zero (the second parameter is unused). src_exponent = exponent - DBL_BIAS. If src_exponent > DBL_FX_MAX_EXP and the value is not exactly the minimum integer (that is src_exponent > DBL_FX_MAX_EXP + 1, or the mantissa is non-zero, or the sign is clear), it is an overflow: the result is 0x7fffffffffffffff for a sign-clear source or 0x8000000000000000 for a sign-set source; the function returns INVALIDEXCEPTION without writing if the invalid trap is enabled, else sets the invalid flag, writes the result and returns NOEXCEPTION. Otherwise, if src_exponent >= 0 it writes the mantissa shifted to an integer (negated by setting the sign for a negative source) and, if the conversion lost bits, returns INEXACTEXCEPTION when the inexact trap is enabled (result already written) or sets the inexact flag. If src_exponent < 0 (the absolute value is less than 1) it writes 0 and, if the source is non-zero, handles inexact the same way. The last return is NOEXCEPTION. No lock or reference is taken.
note: Listed name dbl_to_dint does not exist: the slice is the tail of dbl_to_dbl_fcnvfxt (fcnvfxt.c:~246-315), head read from the real file. Reviewer round 15 right: the exponent test is on the unbiased exponent (src_exponent = Dbl_exponent - DBL_BIAS, slice line 2), so the old wording about a negative biased exponent was wrong.

name: dbl_to_dbl_fcnvuf
prose: Function dbl_to_dbl_fcnvuf(srcptr, _nullptr, dstptr, status) converting the 64-bit unsigned integer at srcptr to a double stored at dstptr (the second parameter is unused). If the source is 0 it stores +0.0 and returns NOEXCEPTION. Otherwise it finds the most significant set bit (searching the high word, or the low word if the high word is 0), left-justifies the source, builds the double mantissa from the top bits and the exponent as (62 + DBL_BIAS) minus the bit offset, with the bits that do not fit left in srcp2. If those remaining bits are non-zero (Duint_isinexact_to_dbl), the result is adjusted by rounding mode: ROUNDPLUS increments the result, ROUNDMINUS leaves it, ROUNDNEAREST applies the nearest rounding derived from the remaining bits, and any other mode (ROUNDZERO) leaves it; then if the inexact trap is enabled it stores the result and returns INEXACTEXCEPTION, otherwise it sets the inexact flag. Otherwise (or after the flag is set) it stores the result and returns NOEXCEPTION. No lock or reference is taken.

name: dbl_fmpynfadd
prose: Function dbl_fmpynfadd(src1ptr, src2ptr, src3ptr, status, dstptr) computing the negated fused multiply-add -(src1 * src2) + src3 in double precision and storing it at dstptr (the initial result sign is the opposite of the sign of src1 times src2). It returns an int exception code using the OPC_2E_ variants. Special operands, tested in this order: if src1 is infinity: when src2 and src3 are not NaN, an infinity times zero, or an infinity product combined with an infinite src3 of the opposite sign, is invalid (returns OPC_2E_INVALIDEXCEPTION if the invalid trap is enabled, else sets the invalid flag, stores a quiet NaN and returns NOEXCEPTION), otherwise a signed infinity is stored (NOEXCEPTION); if src1 is a NaN: a signaling src1 returns OPC_2E_INVALIDEXCEPTION when the invalid trap is enabled, else is quieted with the flag set; a signaling src2 or src3 (checked in that order) is quieted and stored under the same trap rule; otherwise src1 is stored (NOEXCEPTION). The same checks are made for src2 (infinity times a zero src1 stores a quiet NaN made from src2; infinite src3 of opposite sign is invalid; else infinity; a NaN src2 is quieted or stored with the src3 signaling check). If src3 is infinity it is stored; a NaN src3 is quieted (trap or flag when signaling) and stored; all with NOEXCEPTION. If src1 or src2 is zero the product is zero: when src3 is zero the result is src3 with its sign set from the signs (OR with the product sign for ROUNDMINUS, AND otherwise) and stored with NOEXCEPTION; else if src3 is denormal and the underflow trap is enabled it is normalised, given a wrapped exponent, stored and OPC_2E_UNDERFLOWEXCEPTION returned; else src3 is stored with NOEXCEPTION. Denormal non-zero src1 and src2 are normalised. The product mantissa is formed by a four-bit-per-pass shift-and-add loop in a four-word extended format (mpy_exponent = e1 + e2 - DBL_BIAS, incremented if the product overflows its hidden bit). If src3 is zero the product itself is the result and goes to rounding; otherwise a denormal src3 is normalised, the two values are ordered by magnitude (swapped with sign handling), the smaller is right-aligned by the exponent difference (limited to DBLEXT_THRESHOLD) and the magnitudes are subtracted when the signs differ (an exact zero result is stored, negative for ROUNDMINUS, with NOEXCEPTION; the result is renormalised and result_exponent reduced) or added (renormalised on hidden overflow). Rounding: if the result exponent is not positive and the underflow trap is disabled the extended result is denormalised (is_tiny); if the low extension words are non-zero it is inexact and is rounded by the rounding mode, incrementing the exponent on hidden overflow. If result_exponent >= DBL_INFINITY_EXPONENT: with the overflow trap enabled the wrapped-exponent result is stored and OPC_2E_OVERFLOWEXCEPTION returned (| OPC_2E_INEXACTEXCEPTION if inexact and the inexact trap is enabled; if inexact with the trap off the inexact flag is set); with the trap disabled it sets the overflow flag, stores the overflow value and treats it as inexact. If result_exponent <= 0: with the underflow trap enabled the wrapped-exponent result is stored and OPC_2E_UNDERFLOWEXCEPTION returned (| OPC_2E_INEXACTEXCEPTION on the same rule); otherwise the underflow flag is set if inexact and tiny. Otherwise the exponent is stored. The result is stored at dstptr; if inexact it returns OPC_2E_INEXACTEXCEPTION when the inexact trap is enabled else sets the inexact flag; the final return is NOEXCEPTION. The trap-return paths for invalid operands store no result.

The same function is described in the entry for the other slice (1085-1359). Sign handling checked: the initial result sign is cleared when sign1 differs from sign2, i.e. the product is negated.

name: fpudispatch
prose: Function fpudispatch(ir, excp_code, holder, fpregs) that dispatches an FP emulation trap; holder is not used. It first calls parisc_linux_get_fpu_type(fpregs), which overwrites fpregs[FPU_TYPE_FLAG_POS] with TIMEX_EXTEN_FLAG if boot_cpu_data.cpu_type is pcxs, ROLEX_EXTEN_FLAG if it is pcxt or pcxt_, PA2_0_FPU_FLAG if it is pcxu or later, and leaves it unchanged otherwise; it then reads that slot as fpu_type_flags. class = get_class(ir); if class is 1 subop is the 3-bit PA2.0 field when fpu_type_flags has PA2_0_FPU_FLAG and the 2-bit PA1.1 field otherwise, else subop is the 3-bit generic field. It returns decode_0c(ir, class, subop, fpregs) for excp_code MAJOR_0C_EXCP or PA83_UNIMP_EXCP; decode_0e(ir, class, subop, fpregs) for MAJOR_0E_EXCP; decode_06(ir, fpregs) for MAJOR_06_EXCP; decode_26(ir, fpregs) for MAJOR_26_EXCP; decode_2e(ir, fpregs) for MAJOR_2E_EXCP; and UNIMPLEMENTEDEXCEPTION for any other excp_code value (the comment states the emulator must never panic the kernel on odd values). The only non-local state change is the overwrite of the type flag slot, apart from what the decode helpers do.
note: Prose of the old text was checked line by line against fpudispatch.c:181-234 and agrees (the original rejection about the fpregs overwrite and round 2 about arbitrary excp_code are both reflected). No change of substance; wording tightened.

name: decode_0e
prose: Static function decode_0e(ir, class, subop, fpregs) that decodes and emulates a major-0E floating point instruction; it returns the result of an emulation helper, NOEXCEPTION, MAJOR_0E_EXCP (an invalid or unsupported encoding) or MAJOR_0C_EXCP. status is &fpregs[0] and local_status a copy of fpregs[0]. r1 and t are the source and target register numbers taken from ir (r1 == 0 is replaced by fpzeroreg); it returns MAJOR_0E_EXCP if t == 0 and class != 2; fmt is a 2-bit field for class 0 and 1 and a 1-bit field otherwise; for a double format r1 is made even, and t too unless class is 1. Class 0: subop 0 or 1 returns MAJOR_0E_EXCP; subops 2 (copy), 3 (abs, clears the sign bit), 6 (negate) and 7 (negate-abs) return MAJOR_0E_EXCP for fmt 2 or 3, otherwise write the target (for double also the second word) and return NOEXCEPTION; subop 4 returns sgl_fsqrt or dbl_fsqrt (MAJOR_0E_EXCP for fmt 2 or 3); subop 5 returns sgl_frnd or dbl_frnd (same). Class 1 (conversions): df is taken from ir; if df or fmt has bit 2 set it returns MAJOR_0E_EXCP; fmt becomes (fmt << 1) | df; subop 0 returns sgl_to_dbl_fcnvff or dbl_to_sgl_fcnvff for fmt 1 or 2 and MAJOR_0E_EXCP for fmt 0 or 3; subops 1, 2, 3, 5, 6 and 7 return the matching sgl/dbl-to-sgl/dbl conversion (fcnvxf, fcnvfx, fcnvfxt, fcnvuf, fcnvfu, fcnvfut); subop 4 returns MAJOR_0C_EXCP. Class 2 (compare): r2 is taken from ir (fpzeroreg if 0); on a PA2.0 FPU it returns MAJOR_0E_EXCP if the nullify bit is set, otherwise for fmt 0 or 1 it calls sgl_fcmp or dbl_fcmp on local_status with the condition field, calls update_status_cbit(status, local_status, fpu_type_flags, subop) and returns the compare result; on other FPUs subops 1 to 7 return MAJOR_0E_EXCP and subop 0 does the same compare. Class 3 (arithmetic): r2 as above; subops 5 to 7 return MAJOR_0E_EXCP; 0 returns sgl_fadd or dbl_fadd, 1 sgl_fsub or dbl_fsub, 2 sgl_fmpy or dbl_fmpy (if the extension bit is set, MAJOR_0E_EXCP for double or odd t, and for single with even t a BUG()), 3 sgl_fdiv or dbl_fdiv, 4 sgl_frem or dbl_frem. Combinations not matched fall to BUG() calls that are meant to be unreachable, and the final statement returns MAJOR_0E_EXCP.
note: Listed name fpu_emulation_dispatch does not exist: the slice (fpudispatch.c 876-1144) is the middle and end of decode_0e (719-1150), which was read in full; fixed under the real name. Old statement that it returns MAJOR_0E_EXCP/NOEXCEPTION only was incomplete: results come from the helpers and MAJOR_0C_EXCP is also returned.

name: sgl_fdiv
prose: Function sgl_fdiv(srcptr1, srcptr2, dstptr, status) that divides the single at srcptr1 by the single at srcptr2 and stores the result at dstptr. The result sign is the XOR of the operand signs. Special operands, in order: if operand 1 is infinity: when operand 2 is not a NaN, infinity divided by infinity is invalid (INVALIDEXCEPTION if the invalid trap is enabled, else sets the invalid flag, stores a quiet NaN and returns NOEXCEPTION), and infinity divided by anything else stores a signed infinity (NOEXCEPTION); if operand 1 is a NaN: a signaling NaN returns INVALIDEXCEPTION if the invalid trap is enabled, otherwise sets the invalid flag and quiets it; else if operand 2 is a signaling NaN the same rule applies to it and operand 2 is stored; otherwise operand 1 is stored; each ends with NOEXCEPTION. If operand 2 is infinity: a signed zero is stored when it is an infinity; a NaN is quieted (trap or flag when signaling) and stored; NOEXCEPTION. If operand 2 is zero: 0/0 is invalid (trap, or flag and quiet NaN stored, NOEXCEPTION); otherwise DIVISIONBYZEROEXCEPTION if that trap is enabled, else it sets the division-by-zero flag, stores a signed infinity and returns NOEXCEPTION. Then dest_exponent = exp1 - exp2 + SGL_BIAS; a zero operand 1 stores a signed zero and returns NOEXCEPTION; denormal operands are normalised with dest_exponent adjusted; the mantissas are divided with a non-restoring loop of up to SGL_P steps giving guard and sticky bits (inexact is guard OR sticky), and when inexact and (dest_exponent > 0 or the underflow trap is enabled) the mantissa is rounded by the rounding mode (ROUNDPLUS, ROUNDMINUS or ROUNDNEAREST) with dest_exponent incremented on hidden-bit overflow. Finalisation (after rounding, with dest_exponent the result exponent): if dest_exponent >= SGL_INFINITY_EXPONENT (overflow) and the overflow trap is enabled it stores the result with a wrapped exponent (Sgl_setwrapped_exponent) and returns OVERFLOWEXCEPTION, or OVERFLOWEXCEPTION | INEXACTEXCEPTION when inexact and the inexact trap is enabled (if inexact with that trap disabled it sets the inexact flag first); with the overflow trap disabled it sets the overflow flag, replaces the result by the overflow value (infinity or largest finite) and treats it as inexact. If dest_exponent <= 0 (underflow) and the underflow trap is enabled it stores the wrapped-exponent result and returns UNDERFLOWEXCEPTION (| INEXACTEXCEPTION by the same rule); with the trap disabled it denormalises (or produces zero), rounds by the rounding mode when inexact and sets the underflow flag if the result is tiny and inexact. Otherwise it stores dest_exponent. The result is stored at dstptr; if inexact it then returns INEXACTEXCEPTION when the inexact trap is enabled and otherwise sets the inexact flag; the last return is NOEXCEPTION. No lock or reference is taken.

name: sgl_fadd
prose: Function sgl_fadd(leftptr, rightptr, dstptr, status) that adds the singles at leftptr and rightptr and stores the sum at dstptr. Specifically for addition, an invalid operation arises when both operands are infinities of opposite sign (save != 0), and an infinite right operand is stored unchanged. Special operands, in order: if left is infinity: when right is not a NaN, infinity combined with an infinity of the other kind that makes the operation invalid is an invalid operation (INVALIDEXCEPTION if the invalid trap is enabled, else it sets the invalid flag, stores a quiet NaN and returns NOEXCEPTION), otherwise left (adjusted for the operation) is stored with NOEXCEPTION; if left is a NaN a signaling NaN returns INVALIDEXCEPTION when the invalid trap is enabled, else is quieted with the invalid flag set; a signaling right is handled the same way and stored; otherwise left is stored; NOEXCEPTION. If right is infinity it is stored (with the operation sign applied); a NaN right is quieted (trap or flag when signaling) and stored; NOEXCEPTION. For finite operands the two are ordered by magnitude (swapping and adjusting signs so that left is not smaller), then: right zero and left zero give a zero whose sign is chosen from the two signs by the rounding mode (ROUNDMINUS ORs them, other modes AND them) with NOEXCEPTION; right zero and left non-zero give left as the exact result with NOEXCEPTION, except that a denormal left with the underflow trap enabled is normalised, given a wrapped exponent, stored and UNDERFLOWEXCEPTION returned; both denormal: the sum or difference is computed exactly (a zero difference is stored as zero, negative for ROUNDMINUS, with NOEXCEPTION; a sum that became normal is stored with NOEXCEPTION; otherwise the normalised wrapped result is stored and UNDERFLOWEXCEPTION returned when the underflow trap is enabled, else the result is stored with NOEXCEPTION). Otherwise right is aligned by the exponent difference (limited to SGL_THRESHOLD) into an extension word and the magnitudes are added or subtracted according to the effective sign. For a subtraction it renormalises: an exact zero is stored (negative for ROUNDMINUS) with NOEXCEPTION; if the exponent falls to zero or below it returns UNDERFLOWEXCEPTION with a wrapped exponent when the underflow trap is enabled, else the exact denormalised result with NOEXCEPTION; if renormalisation finishes with a valid exponent and the extension is zero the result is stored with NOEXCEPTION, otherwise it continues to rounding. For an addition it shifts right by one on hidden overflow and increments the exponent. Rounding: if the extension is non-zero the result is inexact and is rounded by the rounding mode (nearest-even, up, down or truncate), incrementing the exponent on hidden overflow. If the result exponent equals SGL_INFINITY_EXPONENT: with the overflow trap enabled the wrapped result is stored and OVERFLOWEXCEPTION returned (| INEXACTEXCEPTION if inexact and the inexact trap is enabled, else the inexact flag is set); with the trap disabled it sets the overflow flag, stores the overflow value and treats it as inexact. Otherwise the exponent is stored. The result is stored at dstptr; if inexact it returns INEXACTEXCEPTION when the inexact trap is enabled else sets the inexact flag; the final return is NOEXCEPTION.
note: Listed name for this slice (sfadd.c 261-505) is not in the source: the slice is the tail of sgl_fadd (sfadd.c:~36-505), fixed under the real name after reading the head; differences between add and subtract checked by diffing sfadd.c with sfsub.c (sign inversions and the save test).

name: sgl_fsub
prose: Function sgl_fsub(leftptr, rightptr, dstptr, status) that computes left minus right for the singles at leftptr and rightptr and stores the result at dstptr. Specifically for subtraction, an invalid operation arises when both operands are infinities of the same sign (save == 0) and an infinite right operand is stored with its sign inverted; the sign of right (and of the swapped left) is inverted where the operands are ordered or both are zero, and the effective operation is a magnitude subtraction when the signs are equal. Special operands, in order: if left is infinity: when right is not a NaN, infinity combined with an infinity of the other kind that makes the operation invalid is an invalid operation (INVALIDEXCEPTION if the invalid trap is enabled, else it sets the invalid flag, stores a quiet NaN and returns NOEXCEPTION), otherwise left (adjusted for the operation) is stored with NOEXCEPTION; if left is a NaN a signaling NaN returns INVALIDEXCEPTION when the invalid trap is enabled, else is quieted with the invalid flag set; a signaling right is handled the same way and stored; otherwise left is stored; NOEXCEPTION. If right is infinity it is stored (with the operation sign applied); a NaN right is quieted (trap or flag when signaling) and stored; NOEXCEPTION. For finite operands the two are ordered by magnitude (swapping and adjusting signs so that left is not smaller), then: right zero and left zero give a zero whose sign is chosen from the two signs by the rounding mode (ROUNDMINUS ORs them, other modes AND them) with NOEXCEPTION; right zero and left non-zero give left as the exact result with NOEXCEPTION, except that a denormal left with the underflow trap enabled is normalised, given a wrapped exponent, stored and UNDERFLOWEXCEPTION returned; both denormal: the sum or difference is computed exactly (a zero difference is stored as zero, negative for ROUNDMINUS, with NOEXCEPTION; a sum that became normal is stored with NOEXCEPTION; otherwise the normalised wrapped result is stored and UNDERFLOWEXCEPTION returned when the underflow trap is enabled, else the result is stored with NOEXCEPTION). Otherwise right is aligned by the exponent difference (limited to SGL_THRESHOLD) into an extension word and the magnitudes are added or subtracted according to the effective sign. For a subtraction it renormalises: an exact zero is stored (negative for ROUNDMINUS) with NOEXCEPTION; if the exponent falls to zero or below it returns UNDERFLOWEXCEPTION with a wrapped exponent when the underflow trap is enabled, else the exact denormalised result with NOEXCEPTION; if renormalisation finishes with a valid exponent and the extension is zero the result is stored with NOEXCEPTION, otherwise it continues to rounding. For an addition it shifts right by one on hidden overflow and increments the exponent. Rounding: if the extension is non-zero the result is inexact and is rounded by the rounding mode (nearest-even, up, down or truncate), incrementing the exponent on hidden overflow. If the result exponent equals SGL_INFINITY_EXPONENT: with the overflow trap enabled the wrapped result is stored and OVERFLOWEXCEPTION returned (| INEXACTEXCEPTION if inexact and the inexact trap is enabled, else the inexact flag is set); with the trap disabled it sets the overflow flag, stores the overflow value and treats it as inexact. Otherwise the exponent is stored. The result is stored at dstptr; if inexact it returns INEXACTEXCEPTION when the inexact trap is enabled else sets the inexact flag; the final return is NOEXCEPTION.
note: Listed name for this slice (sfsub.c 264-508) is not in the source: the slice is the tail of sgl_fsub (sfsub.c:~36-508), fixed under the real name after reading the head; the differences from sgl_fadd were found by diffing the two files (three Sgl_invert_sign calls, save == 0 versus != 0, and save >= 0 versus < 0).

name: cpm_console_init
prose: Function cpm_console_init(devp, scdp) of the powerpc boot wrapper that sets up a CPM serial console for the device tree node devp. It sets is_smc and is_cpm2 from the node compatible strings (cpm1-smc-uart: smc; cpm2-scc-uart: cpm2; cpm2-smc-uart: both; otherwise both stay 0), selects the global enable_port and disable_port functions (SMC or SCC variants) and do_cmd (cpm2_cmd or cpm1_cmd). It returns -1 if getprop(devp, "fsl,cpm-command") gives less than 4 bytes, if dt_get_virtual_reg(devp, vreg, 2) gives fewer than 2 entries, if the node has no parent, if the parent has no virtual reg (cpcr), or if finddevice("/soc/cpm/muram/data") returns NULL; these returns happen after the globals above and smc or scc and param were already set. Then, in the part shown: it returns -1 if dt_get_virtual_reg(muram, &muram_addr, 1) gives less than 1 or getprop(muram, "reg", reg, 8) gives less than 8 bytes; otherwise it takes muram_offset = reg[0] and muram_size = reg[1] and computes cbd_offset = muram_offset + muram_size - 2 * sizeof(struct cpm_bd). When is_cpm2 and is_smc are both set it computes pram_offset = cbd_offset - 64 aligned down to 64, calls disable_port(), writes pram_offset with out_be16 to the old parameter RAM pointer and sets param to muram_addr - muram_offset + pram_offset. It then sets cbd_addr = muram_addr - muram_offset + cbd_offset, installs scdp->open, putc, getc and tstc as cpm_serial_open, cpm_serial_putc, cpm_serial_getc and cpm_serial_tstc, and returns 0.
note: Listed name cpm_serial_init is not in the source: the slice is the tail of cpm_console_init (cpm-serial.c:199-295), head read from the real file. The old prose said scdp is unmodified on the -1 returns, which is true, but it omitted that globals were already changed before those returns, and the earlier -1 paths.

name: of_claim
prose: Function of_claim(virt, size, align) that claims memory through Open Firmware and returns an unsigned int. On the first call (need_map < 0) it stores check_of_version() in need_map; check_of_version looks for old Open Firmware (it returns 1 only for a model string starting with "Open Firmware, 1." or "FirmWorks,3." and a found /chosen mmu and /memory node, and in that case sets chosen_mmu and memory; otherwise it returns 0). If align is non-zero or need_map is 0 it returns of_call_prom("claim", 3, 1, virt, size, align): PROM_ERROR if the firmware call itself fails, otherwise the first returned value. Otherwise (align is 0 and need_map non-zero) it makes a call-method "claim" on memory; if that call fails or its result is -1 it returns -1 (0xffffffff); then it calls "claim" on chosen_mmu and "map" on chosen_mmu (coherent read/write mapping of virt to virt), ignoring the status of both, and returns virt as an unsigned int. The arguments reach firmware through varargs read as prom_arg_t (u32), so only the low 32 bits of virt, size and align are used; the service name pointer is converted with ADDR.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: ADDR only converts the service string pointer; virt, size and align are passed as varargs read back as prom_arg_t (oflib.c:39 and of_call_prom), so the 32-bit truncation comes from prom_arg_t, not ADDR. Round 2 right: check_of_version only returns a value (it also sets chosen_mmu and memory) and of_claim assigns need_map. Slice 152-173; callees read at oflib.c:41-150.

name: ATOMIC64_OPS(add, add)
prose: Generated function arch_atomic64_add_return_relaxed(s64 a, atomic64_t *v) (static inline, from ATOMIC64_OP_RETURN_RELAXED(add, add) inside ATOMIC64_OPS(add, add); powerpc64 only). It runs a load-reserve/store-conditional loop (ldarx, add, stdcx., retry with bne- until the store succeeds) that atomically replaces v->counter by v->counter + a, and returns that new value as an s64. The asm has only a "cc" clobber, so no memory barrier is implied (relaxed ordering). It takes no lock.
note: Macro-generated (powerpc/include/asm/atomic.h:230-246, instantiated at line 270 of the real file, ATOMIC64_OPS(add, add)). Old prose accurate; the 2^64 wrap and ordering statements are consistent with the asm.

It runs a load-reserve/store-conditional loop (ldarx, add into a second register, stdcx., retry until the store succeeds) that atomically replaces v->counter by v->counter + a and returns the value v->counter had before the update. The asm has only a "cc" clobber, so no memory barrier is implied (relaxed ordering). It takes no lock.

name: vsid_scramble
prose: Static inline function vsid_scramble(protovsid, vsid_multiplier, vsid_bits) (the active definition, in the #else branch; the #if 0 branch only contains macro alternatives). With vsid_modulus = (1UL << vsid_bits) - 1 it computes vsid = protovsid * vsid_multiplier (an unsigned long product that wraps modulo 2^64), folds it with vsid = (vsid >> vsid_bits) + (vsid & vsid_modulus), and returns (vsid + ((vsid + 1) >> vsid_bits)) & vsid_modulus. The result is in 0 to vsid_modulus and equals the product modulo vsid_modulus (with a multiple of the modulus giving 0) when the arguments are in the range the comment describes (below 2^VSID_BITS) so that the first fold leaves a value below twice the modulus; for other inputs it is just the value given by the three steps above. vsid_bits must be less than 64. It reads no memory and has no side effects.
note: Contract left empty: the earlier contracts failed random testing (they assumed the plain modulo equivalence and negative inputs for unsigned parameters). The old prose claimed equality with product modulo (2^bits - 1) for any product that does not wrap, which only holds in the range the source comment states; now qualified. Source mmu-hash.h:753-763.

name: XCHG_GEN(type, sfx, cl)
prose: Template macro XCHG_GEN(type, sfx, cl) that defines static inline u32 __xchg_<type><sfx>(volatile void *p, u32 val); when CONFIG_PPC_HAS_LBARX_LHARX is not set it is instantiated for __xchg_u8_local, __xchg_u8_relaxed, __xchg_u16_local and __xchg_u16_relaxed (the "local" ones with a "memory" clobber, the "relaxed" ones with only "cc"). Each generated function exchanges a 1- or 2-byte field using a word-sized reservation: off = (unsigned long)p % 4 and bitoff = BITOFF_CAL(sizeof(type), off) (byte position counted from the most significant end on big-endian builds, from the least significant on little-endian); p is rounded down to the aligned 4-byte word; val is shifted left by bitoff and prev_mask = ((u32)(type)-1) << bitoff. In a lwarx/stwcx. loop it clears the mask bits of the loaded word, ORs in the shifted val (val is not masked to the field width, so bits of val beyond the field width would land in neighbouring bytes of the word) and stores, retrying until the store succeeds. It returns prev >> bitoff, the whole old word shifted down, so the caller must truncate to the field type to get the old field value. No barrier is issued apart from the clobber.
note: Macro-generated; name is the definition head (cmpxchg.h:16-38, instantiated at 81-84). Old prose said the field is replaced by the low bits of val; the code does not mask val, so that claim was qualified.

name: CMPXCHG_GEN(type, sfx, br, br2, cl)
prose: Template macro CMPXCHG_GEN(type, sfx, br, br2, cl) that defines static inline u32 __cmpxchg_<type><sfx>(volatile void *p, u32 old, u32 new); it is instantiated (cmpxchg.h:273-280) for u8 and u16 with no suffix (barriers PPC_ATOMIC_ENTRY_BARRIER before and PPC_ATOMIC_EXIT_BARRIER after), _local (no barriers), _acquire (PPC_ACQUIRE_BARRIER after) and _relaxed (no barriers, only a "cc" clobber). Each generated function works on a 1- or 2-byte field through a word-sized reservation: off = (unsigned long)p % 4, bitoff = BITOFF_CAL(sizeof(type), off), p is rounded down to the aligned word, old and new are shifted left by bitoff (not masked to the field width) and prev_mask = ((u32)(type)-1) << bitoff. After the br sequence, in a lwarx/stwcx. loop it loads the word, masks it with prev_mask and compares with the shifted old; if they differ it branches past the br2 sequence to the end, with the word unchanged; if equal it replaces the field with the shifted new (clearing the mask bits then ORing new) and stores, retrying until the store succeeds, and then executes br2. It returns prev >> bitoff, the loaded word shifted down, which the caller truncates to the field type: the old field value on success and the current field value on a mismatch. On a mismatch the br2 (exit barrier or acquire barrier) is skipped.
note: Macro-generated; name is the definition head (cmpxchg.h:40-71). Added that the br2 barrier is skipped on the failure path (the 2: label comes after br2) and that old and new are not masked.

name: btext_find_display
prose: Function btext_find_display(allow_nonstdout), __init, that selects a boot text display. It starts with np = of_stdout and rc = -ENODEV; if of_stdout is not a node of type "display" it prints a message and np becomes NULL; if np is set rc = btext_initialize(np) (which returns 0 on success and -EINVAL if a width, height or depth property is missing or the framebuffer address is 0). It returns rc at once if rc is 0 or allow_nonstdout is 0 (so -ENODEV when stdout is not a display, -EINVAL when it is a display but initialisation failed, 0 on success). Otherwise it loops over all "display" nodes with for_each_node_by_type: for a node having the "linux,opened" property it prints, calls btext_initialize on it and prints the result; if rc is 0 it calls of_node_put on the node and leaves the loop, so the reference the iterator holds is released. It returns the final rc: 0 on success, otherwise the result of the last attempt (-EINVAL), or the earlier value (-ENODEV or -EINVAL) if no node was tried. Return values are therefore 0, -EINVAL or -ENODEV.
note: Contract cleared (globals and device-tree state). Old prose accurate; reviewers only said the formal contract omitted the error codes. Callee btext_initialize read at btext.c:160-219 (returns only 0 or -EINVAL). Slice 221-247.

name: fadump_locate_reserve_mem
prose: Static __init function fadump_locate_reserve_mem(base, size) that looks for a free memory area of at least size bytes that does not overlap the firmware reserved ranges (reserved_mrange_info). It iterates over all free memblock ranges [mstart, mend); for each, if mstart > base it sets base = PAGE_ALIGN(mstart) (so base carries over from earlier ranges and only moves forward when a later range starts above it). While mend > base and mend - base >= size it calls overlaps_reserved_ranges(base, base + size, &idx): if there is no overlap it returns base; otherwise it sets base to PAGE_ALIGN(the end of reserved range idx) and tries again within the same free range. If no free range yields a fitting non-overlapping interval it returns 0. The returned address is therefore the input base (not necessarily page aligned, when that value is already inside a free range), or a PAGE_ALIGN-ed free-range start, or a PAGE_ALIGN-ed reserved-range end; the interval [r, r + size) lies inside one free range and does not overlap any reserved range. It allocates nothing and takes no lock; size is not checked for 0.
note: Reviewer round 2 and 15 are consistent with the old prose, which already said the candidates are PAGE_ALIGN-ed free-range starts or reserved-range ends, and gave no alignment guarantee; the new wording states that explicitly and that base carries across free ranges. Slice 8-37 (the head comment lines are part of the slice).

name: apply_relocate_add
prose: Function apply_relocate_add(sechdrs, strtab, symindex, relsec, me) that applies the SHT_RELA relocations of section relsec to the section named by its sh_info for module me. Unless CONFIG_PPC_KERNEL_PCREL is set it first, once per module (me->arch.toc_fixed), sets the .TOC. symbol value from my_r2. Then for each Elf64_Rela it computes location = target section address + r_offset, the symbol, and value = sym->st_value + r_addend, and switches on the relocation type: ADDR32, ADDR64, TOC, REL64, REL32, the 16-bit TOC and REL16 forms, ENTRY, TOCSAVE and (with PCREL) GOT_PCREL34 and PCREL34 write the computed value into the location; unknown types print "Unknown ADD relocation" and return -ENOEXEC. Returns while processing: -ENOEXEC for an out-of-range or misaligned TOC16, TOC16_DS, TOC16_LO_DS, REL24 or REL32 (or PCREL34 outside a per-cpu section) value, or if restore_r2 fails; -ENOENT if stub_for_addr (for an undefined or livepatch symbol in REL24/REL24_NOTOC) or got_for_addr returns 0; -EFAULT if patch_instruction fails (REL24 and PCREL34). Relocations processed before a failing one stay applied. Some types are not range checked (ADDR32, ADDR64, REL64, the _LO and REL16 forms), and R_PPC64_ENTRY only rewrites the instruction pair when the instruction pattern matches and the offset fits. If all relocations succeed it returns 0.
note: Reviewer round 15 is wrong: apply_relocate_add does have -EFAULT paths from patch_instruction (module_64.c REL24 and PCREL34 cases, slice seen at the REL24 case in the real file lines ~950-960). The slice cut the head; the whole function was read from the real file (module_64.c:793-1040). The old prose is kept in substance and extended with the exact error sources.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE3(pciconfig_iobase, long, which, unsigned long, bus, unsigned long, devfn)
prose: Generated syscall function sys_pciconfig_iobase (powerpc) taking which, bus and devfn (devfn is not used). It finds the PCI controller whose [first_busno, last_busno] range (inclusive) contains bus with pci_bus_to_hose and returns -ENODEV if none is found. Otherwise it switches on which: IOBASE_BRIDGE_NUMBER returns (long)hose->first_busno, IOBASE_MEMORY returns (long)hose->mem_offset[0], IOBASE_IO returns (long)hose->io_base_phys, IOBASE_ISA_IO returns (long)isa_io_base, IOBASE_ISA_MEM returns (long)isa_mem_base, and any other value falls out of the switch and returns -EOPNOTSUPP. It takes no lock (the hose list is walked without locking in this code).
note: Macro-generated function; name is the SYSCALL_DEFINE3 invocation (pci_32.c:65-89). Old prose accurate; added that devfn is unused and the lookup is unlocked.

name: __switch_to
prose: Function __switch_to(prev, new) of powerpc: it does the architecture part of a context switch and returns the task that was running before the switch (the value returned by _switch). It uses new_thread = &new->thread and old_thread = &current->thread and warns (WARN_ON) if interrupts are enabled. With CONFIG_PPC_64S_HASH_MMU: if the per-cpu TLB batch is active it sets _TLF_LAZY_MMU in the current thread info, calls __flush_tlb_pending if the batch has entries and clears batch->active; and if new->mm is set and (the CPU has CPU_FTR_ARCH_31 or new->mm->context.vas_windows is non-zero) it executes cp_abort. It then switches the breakpoint or debug registers for new (switch_booke_debug_regs, or switch_hw_breakpoint when not using hw breakpoints), calls save_sprs(&prev->thread), giveup_all(prev) (saving FPU, Altivec, VSX and SPE state) and __switch_to_tm(prev, new); if radix is not enabled it calls hard_irq_disable(); it calls restore_sprs(old_thread, new_thread) and set_return_regs_changed() before _switch, and on non-Book3S-64 kernels kuap_assert_locked(). It then calls last = _switch(old_thread, new_thread). After _switch returns (this code does not run for newly created tasks, which return through the fork path), on Book3S-64 with the hash MMU, if the now-current thread has _TLF_LAZY_MMU set it clears the flag and sets the per-cpu batch active again; and on Book3S-64, if current->thread.regs is set it calls restore_math(current->thread.regs). It returns last. It takes no lock.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: the cp_abort condition is new->mm && (CPU_FTR_ARCH_31 || vas_windows), not only foreign real mappings (process.c slice lines 24-26; also only for the hash MMU build). Slice cut the head; read signature at process.c:1284-1289.

name: copy_thread
prose: Function copy_thread(p, args) that sets up the architecture state of a new task p from the clone arguments. It calls klp_init_thread_info(p) and starts at the top of p kernel stack. For a kernel thread (p->flags has PF_KTHREAD) it reserves a minimal stack frame, selects f = start_kernel_thread as the first function to run, sets p->thread.regs to NULL and clears the compat flag. For a user thread it reserves an interrupt frame with the regs marker: if args->fn is set (a user thread that first runs a kernel function) the child pt_regs are zeroed (softe = IRQS_ENABLED on PPC64) and f = ret_from_kernel_user_thread; otherwise the child pt_regs are copied from current_pt_regs(), gpr[1] is set to args->stack if non-zero, with CLONE_SETTLS the TLS value goes in gpr[13] (gpr[2] for a 32-bit task), and f is ret_from_fork_scv if the parent trap was a system call vector else ret_from_fork; for both user cases MSR_FP, MSR_VEC and MSR_VSX are cleared in the child regs and p->thread.regs points to them. It then builds a switch frame: the link save slot is set to f, the frame regs get nip = ppc_function_entry(f), and when args->fn is set gpr[14] and gpr[15] receive the kernel function entry and args->fn_arg; p->thread.ksp is set to the new stack pointer. It then clears (as configured) the hardware breakpoint slots, the FP and Altivec save-area pointers and the KUAP or pid state, calls setup_ksp_vsid, on PPC64 copies dscr_inherit from the current thread, reads the DSCR register into p->thread.dscr when the CPU has CPU_FTR_DSCR, and zeros tidr; on Book3S-64 it copies hashkeyr from the current thread if the CPU has the DEXCR NPHIE feature and reads the DEXCR register into p->thread.dexcr if it has CPU_FTR_ARCH_31. It returns 0 on its only return path.
note: Reviewer round 15 is wrong: the kernel-thread entry is start_kernel_thread in the code (process.c:1758-1775, f = start_kernel_thread); the comment further down still uses the old name ret_from_kernel_thread. The old prose was otherwise checked against the real file and kept; head read from lines 1758-1800.

name: rtas_get_sensor_fast
prose: Function rtas_get_sensor_fast(sensor, index, state) that reads an RTAS sensor without retrying on busy status. It looks up the token of the get-sensor-state function and returns -ENOENT if it is RTAS_UNKNOWN_SERVICE (no call made, *state not written). Otherwise it makes one rtas_call(token, 2, 2, state, sensor, index) and takes the status rc it returns. It issues WARN_ON if rc is RTAS_BUSY (-2) or in the extended-delay range 9900 to 9905. If rc is negative it returns rtas_error_rc(rc): -EIO for -1 (hardware error), -EINVAL for -3 (invalid parameter), -EFAULT, -EEXIST or -ENODEV for -9000, -9001 and -9002, and -ERANGE (with a printed message) for any other negative value, which includes RTAS_BUSY. If rc is not negative, including the positive extended-delay values, it returns rc unchanged. *state holds the output the RTAS call stored there.
note: Reviewer rounds 1, 2 and 15 right: extended-delay hints (9900-9905) are positive and are returned unchanged after the WARN_ON, only negative statuses go through rtas_error_rc; RTAS_BUSY (-2) is negative and so is mapped to -ERANGE. Old prose wrongly said the extended-delay hints map to -ERANGE. rtas_error_rc read in rtas.c; slice 133-148.

name: rtas_set_indicator_fast
prose: Function rtas_set_indicator_fast(indicator, index, new_value) that sets an RTAS indicator without retrying on busy status. It looks up the token of the set-indicator function and returns -ENOENT if it is RTAS_UNKNOWN_SERVICE (no call made). Otherwise it makes one rtas_call(token, 3, 1, NULL, indicator, index, new_value) and takes the status rc. It issues WARN_ON if rc is RTAS_BUSY (-2) or in the extended-delay range 9900 to 9905. If rc is negative it returns rtas_error_rc(rc): -EIO for -1, -EINVAL for -3, -EFAULT, -EEXIST or -ENODEV for -9000, -9001 and -9002, and -ERANGE for any other negative value (including RTAS_BUSY). If rc is not negative, including the positive extended-delay values, it returns rc unchanged.
note: Reviewer rounds 1, 2 and 15 right: positive extended-delay statuses are returned unchanged, not mapped to -ERANGE; RTAS_BUSY is negative and mapped to -ERANGE. Slice 196-213.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE1(rtas, struct rtas_args __user *, uargs)
prose: Generated syscall function sys_rtas taking a user pointer uargs to a struct rtas_args with big-endian fields. It returns -EPERM if the caller lacks CAP_SYS_ADMIN; -EINVAL if rtas.entry is 0; -EFAULT if copying the 3-word header fails. It then reads nargs, nret and token from the header and returns -EINVAL if nargs >= ARRAY_SIZE(args.args), nret > ARRAY_SIZE(args.args) or nargs + nret > ARRAY_SIZE(args.args) (that array has 16 entries). It copies nargs argument words from user space (-EFAULT on failure), maps the token to a known function with rtas_token_to_function_untrusted (-EINVAL if unknown), zeroes the nret result words and returns -EINVAL if block_rtas_call rejects the call. For a restricted error-injection token it returns the error from security_locked_down(LOCKDOWN_RTAS_ERROR_INJECTION) if non-zero. For the ibm,suspend-me token it calls rtas_syscall_dispatch_ibm_suspend_me(handle): -EAGAIN sets the first result word to RTAS_NOT_SUSPENDABLE and -EIO sets it to -1, both going on to copy the results out; any other non-zero return value is returned directly (no copy-out); 0 goes on to the copy-out. For all other tokens it takes an error-log buffer, takes the function mutex if the function has one, takes rtas_lock with interrupts saved, runs do_enter_rtas on a copy of the arguments, fetches the last error log if the first result word is -1, releases rtas_lock and the mutex, logs the error and frees the buffer, and continues to the copy-out. The copy-out copies the nret result words back to user memory and returns -EFAULT if that fails, else 0.
note: Old prose said nargs >= 32; the argument array has 16 entries (asm/rtas-types.h:13), so the limit is 16. Old wording about the suspend-me error path implied a copy-out for every non-zero dispatch error; only -EAGAIN and -EIO reach the copy-out. Macro-generated function: name is the SYSCALL_DEFINE1 invocation (rtas.c:1850-1971). Slice cut the head; declarations read from the real file.

name: data_read
prose: Static ssize_t data_read(filep, kobj, attr, buf, off, count), the read method of the secvar "data" binary sysfs attribute. It calls secvar_ops->get(kobj->name, strlen(kobj->name) + 1, NULL, &dsize) to get the variable size; if that returns non-zero it returns that value unchanged (printing an error unless it is -ENOENT) without allocating anything. It then kzallocs dsize bytes and returns -ENOMEM if that fails. It calls secvar_ops->get again to fill the buffer; on failure it prints an error and returns the backend value. Otherwise it returns memory_read_from_buffer(buf, count, &off, data, dsize): -EINVAL if off is negative, 0 (nothing copied, off unchanged) if off >= dsize, else it copies min(count, dsize - off) bytes into buf, advances off by that amount and returns it. The temporary buffer is freed on every path after it was allocated; buf is owned by the caller.
note: The listed name size_probe_then_read does not exist: the slice contains data_read (secvar-sysfs.c:54-85), whose behaviour matches the old prose. Reviewer round 1 (copy when off > dsize) and round 2 (negative off versus get errors) are wrong against that prose: it already says 0 when off >= dsize and puts the backend errors first.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE0(rt_sigreturn)
prose: Generated syscall function sys_rt_sigreturn for 32-bit powerpc (defined by COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE0(rt_sigreturn) on PPC64 builds and SYSCALL_DEFINE0(rt_sigreturn) otherwise), no arguments. It sets current->restart_block.fn = do_no_restart_syscall and takes rt_sf = regs->gpr[1] + __SIGNAL_FRAMESIZE + 16 as a user pointer; if access_ok fails it goes to bad. With transactional memory configured it reclaims suspended transactional state (tm_reclaim_current) if MSR_TM_SUSPENDED, reads the uc_link pointer of the frame (failure goes to bad); if that points to a transactional ucontext it reads its uc_regs pointer and returns -EFAULT immediately, without reporting a fault or sending a signal, if that read fails; then reads the high MSR word from that mcontext (failure goes to bad); if its TM state is active it goes to bad when the CPU has no TM, else restores through do_setcontext_tm (failure goes to bad) and remembers tm_restore. If no TM restore was done it clears MSR_TS_MASK in regs->msr and calls do_setcontext(&rt_sf->uc, regs, 1) (failure goes to bad). It then restores the alternate stack (compat_restore_altstack on PPC64, restore_altstack otherwise; failure goes to bad), sets TIF_RESTOREALL and returns 0. At bad it calls signal_fault(current, regs, "sys_rt_sigreturn", rt_sf), force_sig(SIGSEGV) and returns 0. So the return values are 0, or -EFAULT only for the uc_regs read failure.
note: Old prose agrees with the code (the original rejection about -EFAULT is already in it); wording tightened and the order of checks made explicit. Macro-generated; name is the SYSCALL_DEFINE0 invocation (signal_32.c:1096-1123 in the real file; slice lines 25-124).

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE0(sigreturn)
prose: Generated syscall function sys_sigreturn for 32-bit powerpc (defined by COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE0(sigreturn) on PPC64 builds and SYSCALL_DEFINE0(sigreturn) otherwise), no arguments. It sets current->restart_block.fn = do_no_restart_syscall, takes sf = regs->gpr[1] + __SIGNAL_FRAMESIZE as a user sigframe pointer and copies the sigcontext from it; if that copy fails it goes to badframe. It builds the old signal mask from sigctx.oldmask and the stashed upper bits and installs it with set_current_blocked before restoring registers, so that mask stays installed on the later failures. With transactional memory configured it reads the high MSR word from the transactional mcontext (failure goes to badframe); if the TM state is active it goes to badframe when the CPU has no TM and otherwise restores with restore_tm_user_regs (failure goes to badframe). In the non-TM case it restores the registers from sigctx.regs with restore_user_regs; on failure it calls signal_fault(current, regs, "sys_sigreturn", sr), force_sig(SIGSEGV) and returns 0. On success it sets TIF_RESTOREALL and returns 0. At badframe it calls signal_fault(current, regs, "sys_sigreturn", sc), force_sig(SIGSEGV) and returns 0. Every return is 0.
note: Slice cut the tail; the rest read from the real file (signal_32.c:1296-1360). Old prose accurate; added that the signal mask is installed before the register restore and the full list of failure points. Reviewer round 2 (altstack) is not claimed here. Macro-generated; name is the SYSCALL_DEFINE0 invocation.
